name: Global temperature
state: ERA5 data for 28 Oct put the global surface air temperature about 1.82°C above pre-industrial levels, past the 1.6°C Alert line. The strong El Niño is adding to long-term warming, and 2026 is on course to be among the two warmest years on record.
for_you: Expect more frequent heat and rainfall extremes; follow national weather warnings.

sources.title: MyJoyOnline — 2026 set to be world's second-hottest year

why: Global temperature is the master climate variable; each tenth of a degree raises extreme-weather risk.
drivers: Greenhouse gases, El Niño/La Niña, aerosols, solar cycle.

rubric.alert: > +1.6°C, or a record high for the calendar date.
rubric.normal: Daily global anomaly < +1.3°C above pre-industrial (ERA5 vs 1991–2020 + 0.88°C).
